cards.explanation: The answer is False, friends. The writer says, “Although Jesus had performed so many signs in their presence, they still did not believe in Him.” (John 12:37) Signs piled up and the belief just wasn't there.

The answer is True, friends. The words from Isaiah, the prophet, say they cannot see, understand and turn, “…and I would heal them.” (John 12:40) Healing is right there at the end of the line. It's a short phrase, but it's easy to skim past.

The answer is Jesus, friends. The writer says, “Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus’ glory and spoke about Him.” (John 12:41) Isaiah the prophet was talking about Jesus. That's a whole lot of looking ahead packed into one verse.

The answer is False, friends. The Gospel of John tells us many of the leaders believed in Him, “But because of the Pharisees they did not confess Him…” (John 12:42) The belief was real, but the confessing out loud didn't happen. I think that's a heavy spot to be in.

The answer is being put out of the synagogue, friends. The Pharisees were a strict Jewish religious group, and the writer says the leaders stayed quiet “…for fear that they would be put out of the synagogue.” (John 12:42) That's the fear the text names. It's a quiet kind of pressure, and I think plenty of people feel something like it.

The answer is praise from people, friends. The writer says, “For they loved praise from men more than praise from God.” (John 12:43) It's a plain sentence, and it's easy to see ourselves in it. I know I like a compliment on a good batch.

The answer is the One who sent Him, friends. Jesus cries out, “Whoever believes in Me does not believe in Me alone, but in the One who sent Me.” (John 12:44) Believing in Jesus reaches the One who sent Him too. Jesus names no one else here.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus says, “And whoever sees Me sees the One who sent Me.” (John 12:45) Just before this, He said that believing in Him means believing in the One who sent Him (John 12:44). So looking at Jesus doesn't stop at Jesus. The One being seen is the Father who sent Him (John 12:49).

The answer is darkness, friends. Jesus says, “I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in Me should remain in darkness.” (John 12:46) A light and darkness go together, and I know that dark very well. Believers don't have to stay in it.

The answer is False, friends. Jesus says, “As for anyone who hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him.” (John 12:47) So He says He doesn't judge that person. And then He tells you why in the next part of the verse.

The answer is save, friends. Jesus says, “For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.” (John 12:47) He has just said He doesn't judge the one who hears His words and doesn't keep them. Judging isn't why He came. He came to save.

The answer is the word He has spoken, friends. Jesus says, “The word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.” (John 12:48) The words He has spoken are the judge. Worth reading again slowly.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus says, “I have not spoken on My own, but the Father who sent Me has commanded Me what to say and how to say it.” (John 12:49) The Father gives both the what and the how. That's the whole sentence.
The answer is exactly, friends. Jesus says, “So I speak exactly what the Father has told Me to say.” (John 12:50) Exactly is a strong word. There's no room left for a guess.
